name: Fetal Minoxidil Syndrome

criteria.description: Documented maternal use of minoxidil during pregnancy
Presence of characteristic craniofacial anomalies including cleft lip and palate
Congenital limb defects such as distal limb hypoplasia or oligodactyly
Intrauterine growth retardation or low birth weight

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Confirmed maternal minoxidil exposure plus presence of at least two major congenital anomalies including craniofacial and limb defects
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and based on maternal drug history combined with characteristic congenital malformations.

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; occasional thrombocytopenia
Thyroid function tests may reveal hypothyroidism in rare cases
imaging: Prenatal ultrasound showing limb anomalies and craniofacial defects
Postnatal echocardiography revealing congenital heart defects
Skeletal X-rays demonstrating distal limb hypoplasia
genetic: No known genetic mutation; syndrome caused by teratogenic exposure to minoxidil
other: Maternal history of topical or systemic minoxidil use during pregnancy
Clinical examination revealing characteristic dysmorphic features

distinguishingFeatures: Distinctive facial features including smooth philtrum and thin upper lip

redFlags: Maternal use of minoxidil during pregnancy
Presence of cleft lip and/or palate with limb defects
Congenital heart defects with respiratory distress in neonate
references: Jones KL. Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation. 7th ed. Elsevier; 2013.
Brent RL. Teratogen update: Minoxidil. Teratology. 1995;52(3):153-159.
